content.text:
In the PhET "Build a Nucleus" simulation, configuring a Beryllium nucleus with 4 protons and 2 neutrons gives Beryllium-6 (⁶Be), which is an unstable nuclide with a half-life of approximately 5.0 × 10⁻²¹ seconds.

When proton emission decay occurs:
- Emitted particle: 1 proton (p or ¹₁p)
- Resulting daughter nucleus: Lithium-5 (⁵Li)
  - Protons: 3
  - Neutrons: 2
  - Mass Number: 5
  - Stability: Unstable (half-life of approximately 3.7 × 10⁻²² seconds)

Nuclear decay equation:
⁶₄Be → ⁵₃Li + ¹₁p

In the PhET "Build a Nucleus" simulation, configuring a Beryllium nucleus with 4 protons and 2 neutrons gives Beryllium-6 (⁶Be), which is an unstable nuclide with a half-life of approximately 5.0 × 10⁻²¹ seconds.

When proton emission decay occurs:
- Emitted particle: 1 proton (p or ¹₁p)
- Resulting daughter nucleus: Lithium-5 (⁵Li)
  - Protons: 3
  - Neutrons: 2
  - Mass Number: 5
  - Stability: Unstable (half-life of approximately 3.7 × 10⁻²² seconds)

Nuclear decay equation:
⁶₄Be → ⁵₃Li + ¹₁p
